correctness.rationale: The exact iid geometric likelihood gives the stated MLE including its boundary extension, and comparing integer CDFs gives the survival-count supremum. For nq→∞, expand S/(n+S) about ES to first order: the quadratic remainder in n qhat is O_P(q), while S−A is B plus higher-bin counts. Centered counts from j≥3 sum to the centered sum of (K−2)_+, whose variance is O(nq³). Consequently the first two signed discrepancies have opposite leading terms ±(B−nq²), with O_P(√(nq³)+q) error. For j≥3, conditioning on M=N_3 gives a centered empirical tail process of M geometric excesses with expected count-scale supremum O(√M); the separate binomial fluctuation of M about nq³ is O_P(√(nq³)). The fitted powers change by only O_P(q^(5/2)/√n) at those endpoints. This controls the whole supremum, not merely the zero-frequency contrast. Applying the binomial CLT, Poisson convergence or P(B=0)→1 gives the first three limits with the stated normalizations. When nq stays bounded, B=0 with probability tending to one; there D=A²/[n(n+A)] since the first discrepancy dominates the fitted second tail. This gives the Poisson-square limit and finite-exponent nonexistence probability. Given A=m and B=0, bootstrap higher bins have probability at most n[m/(n+m)]², and outside that event strict increase of the exact statistic in the number of nonzero observations reduces the tie-inclusive p-value to P(Bin(n,m/(n+m))≥m), up to that same error. It tends to π(m), including m=0; tightness of A justifies mixing. The finite checker was inspected, not run, and does not prove these array or bootstrap limits.
residual_risks: No claims for a fitted lower cutoff, moving cutoffs chosen from data, dependence, non-Pareto noise, randomized bootstrap ties, or moment convergence in the sparse window.
